extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) seeking expedited/Track One/prioritized examination before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on eligibility, filing procedures, required fees, termination events, timing, refunds, and RCE-specific rules for requesting prioritized (Track One) examination of U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and goal of prioritized examination (Track One)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritized examination is a procedure for expedited review of a patent application for an additional fee (37 C.F.R. § 1.102(e)). It is also known as 'Track One' or 'Track I'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO’s goal for prioritized examination is to provide a final disposition within twelve months of prioritized status being granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to use PTO/AIA/424 form
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly recommended that applicants use the USPTO’s certification and request form PTO/AIA/424 to request prioritized examination, but the form is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is available on EFS-Web and the USPTO website. Failure to use PTO/AIA/424 could result in the USPTO not recognizing the request or delays. Applicant-created forms should be equivalent to the USPTO form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual limit and availability notices (10,000 grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a fiscal year limit of 10,000 granted requests for prioritized examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO posts statistics (including number granted) on its website and will post a message in EFS-Web when the number is close to the limit. If the limit is reached, the ability to file a request in EFS-Web will be turned off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination fee amounts by entity size
rubrics_metrics.description: The prioritized examination fee under 37 C.F.R. 1.17(c) is $4,000 for a non-small entity, $2,000 for a small entity, and $1,000 for a micro entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required fees to be paid upon filing for Track One (original filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees required to be paid upon filing for Prioritized Examination include the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, publication fee (currently $0), prioritized examination processing fee (37 C.F.R. 1.17(i)(1)), and the prioritized examination fee (37 C.F.R. 1.17(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of the above fees are unpaid at filing, the Request for Prioritized Examination will be dismissed unless an explicit authorization to charge missing fees is provided in the accompanying papers. It is recommended to include such an authorization to avoid dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request dismissal/refund consequences for unpaid or dismissed requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Track One request is dismissed, only the Track One prioritized examination fee (37 C.F.R. 1.17(c)) will be refunded automatically if paid; the Track One processing fee is retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application fees (basic filing, search, examination, and any application size or excess claim fees) generally cannot be refunded. Applicant may petition for express abandonment to request refund of the search fee and any excess claims fees (37 C.F.R. 1.138(d)). Publication fee refunds per MPEP 1126 if not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — types of applications eligible for Track One
rubrics_metrics.description: Original nonprovisional utility and plant patent applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) that have no more than 4 independent claims, no more than 30 total claims, and no multiple dependent claims, and filed on or after September 26, 2011, are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'original application' includes first filings and continuing applications (continuation, continuation-in-part, divisional). Reissue applications are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing method and timing for Track One requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for Prioritized Examination of utility patent applications must be filed using EFS-Web; requests for plant patent applications must be filed on paper. The Request must be present on filing of the utility or plant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an item is inadvertently omitted when filing via EFS-Web, a follow-on submission supplying the missing item may be submitted only on the same day as the filing, and the filer must be a registered EFS-Web user to submit follow-on documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: National/international application and priority-claim rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) that claims the benefit of an earlier international application under 35 U.S.C. 365(c) or the right of priority under 365(a) can be eligible for prioritized examination; a national stage application under 35 U.S.C. 371 (filed as the national stage of an international application) may not have Track One requested at initial national stage filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an earlier international application was not filed in English, a translation is required in accordance with 37 C.F.R. 1.52(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor oath/declaration / ADS requirements on filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper request requires either an executed inventor’s oath/declaration under 37 C.F.R. 1.63 or 1.64 for each inventor, or a signed ADS providing each inventor’s legal name, mailing address, and residence (if not residing at the mailing address) on the date of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joint inventor has refused to execute an oath and a substitute statement is used, the substitute statement and other declarations or a signed ADS must be submitted on filing. If the signed ADS is not present or the substitute statement is defective, prioritized status will not be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication requests and publication fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An application with a nonpublication request may still request prioritized examination; although the publication fee is required by rule, it is currently set to $0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the publication fee is changed in the future, that fee amount must be submitted with the request for prioritized examination even if nonpublication is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for an application to be in condition for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper request for prioritized examination requires that the application include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 including claim(s), any required drawings, an inventor’s oath/declaration or signed ADS, and the required fees (filing, search, examination, prioritized examination fee and processing fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests will be acted upon once the application has met all formal requirements so it is ready for examination (see MPEP 708.02 VIII.C). Failure to submit required items on the date of filing will cause the request to be dismissed. Other informalities (e.g., compliance with 37 C.F.R. 1.52, English-language specification, excess claims fee) will delay a decision but will not cause dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of pre-examination notices and extensions on prioritized status
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-examination notice identifying missing items or informalities will delay a decision on the request until applicant files a complete and timely reply to the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for an extension of time, including to respond to a pre-examination notice, will cause the application to be ineligible for further treatment under the prioritized examination program. A request for extension of time prior to the grant of prioritized status will prevent such status from being granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events that terminate prioritized examination special status
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritized examination status remains until one of several listed events occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events include: (i) filing a petition for extension of time to extend time for filing a reply; (ii) filing an amendment that causes >4 independent claims, >30 total claims, or a multiple dependent claim; (iii) filing a request for continued examination (RCE); (iv) filing a notice of appeal; (v) filing a request for suspension of action; (vi) mailing of a notice of allowance; (vii) mailing of a final Office action; (viii) abandonment of the application; (ix) examination completed as defined in 37 C.F.R. 41.102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected final disposition timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO’s goal is to provide a final disposition within twelve months, on average, of the date that prioritized status was granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition under 37 C.F.R. 1.181 for dismissed requests
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who receives a decision dismissing a request for prioritized examination may file a petition under 37 C.F.R. 1.181 if they believe the dismissal was improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before filing such a petition, applicant should review the reasons stated in the dismissal to determine whether an error was made by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing omitted items same-day via EFS-Web
rubrics_metrics.description: If an item was inadvertently omitted when filing the utility application and the prioritized-exam form via EFS-Web, the applicant may submit a follow-on EFS-Web submission that supplies the missing item only if the follow-on is submitted on the same day as the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only registered EFS-Web users can submit follow-on documents. See MPEP 502.05, III, D. for examples of implications when items are omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment policy for Track One applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment filed in an application that includes a Track One request will not result in dismissal of a pending request or termination of special status if already granted, provided the amendment does not cause the application to contain more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or a multiple dependent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filing policy for Track One applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an information disclosure statement (IDS) in an application with a Track One request will not result in dismissal of a pending request or termination of special status if already granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds and retained fees on dismissal (Track One and RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Track One prioritized examination fee (37 C.F.R. 1.17(c)) will be refunded upon dismissal of the original request; the processing fee (37 C.F.R. 1.17(i)(1)) will be retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request refunds of the search fee and any excess claims fees by filing a petition for express abandonment (37 C.F.R. 1.138(d)). Publication fee refunds may be requested under MPEP 1126 if the application is not published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination availability and rules for RCE filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Original nonprovisional utility and plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111, or which have entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, may request prioritized examination when a proper RCE has been filed (or is concurrently filed), provided prosecution is closed and the application meets the claim limits (≤4 independent, ≤30 total, no multiple dependent claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper RCE can only be filed if prosecution is closed (e.g., last Office action is final, notice of allowance, or otherwise closes prosecution). The Request for Prioritized Examination must be made before an Office action responsive to the RCE has been mailed. Requests for RCE prioritized examination of utility applications must be filed via EFS-Web; plant applications on paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and counting of prioritized examination requests for RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: The 10,000 annual limit applies to the sum of all granted requests (Track One and RCE requests). The program permits a single request to be granted upon filing a new 35 U.S.C. 111(a) application and a single request to be granted upon filing a request for continued examination under 37 C.F.R. 1.114 in that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one prioritized request is permitted associated with a request for continued examination in an application; a second RCE cannot be the subject of a second granted prioritized request in that same application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure after dismissal of a prioritized request for an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for prioritized examination associated with a request for continued examination is dismissed, the applicant may file a petition under 37 C.F.R. 1.181 or may file a new request for prioritized examination for the same RCE, provided the new request includes proper fees and is timely (filed prior to the mailing of the first Office action after filing the RCE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to charge missing fees to avoid dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: If required fees are unpaid at filing, the Request for Prioritized Examination will be dismissed unless an explicit authorization to charge missing fees is provided in the papers accompanying the application/request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing authorization to charge additional fees under 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.16 and 1.17 is recommended to ensure a Track One request is not dismissed for failure to pay required fees.
